facts.statement: The Board has 10 directors: all 10 nominees (Burke, Bammann, Combs, Crown, Dimon, Flynn, Hobson, Neal, Novakovic, Rometty) are current directors, and all directors are elected annually.
10 directors were serving on the Board at the time of the 2021 annual meeting.

Nine of ten directors are independent (all except CEO James Dimon): after reviewing ordinary-course credit and goods/services relationships, the Board determined each non-management director (Bammann, Burke, Combs, Crown, Flynn, Hobson, Neal, Novakovic, Rometty) independent under NYSE and Firm standards.
All directors who served on the Audit Committee and the CMDC were determined to meet the additional NYSE independence and qualitative criteria for those committees.
The five principal standing committees are 100% independent, and each Board committee is chaired and constituted by independent directors.
The Board has five principal standing committees: Audit, Compensation & Management Development (CMDC), Corporate Governance & Nominating (Governance), Public Responsibility (PRC) and Risk.
The Board has two additional standing committees: the Stock Committee and the Executive Committee.
The Board currently has two Specific Purpose Committees, the Markets Compliance Committee and the Omnibus Committee, which were also its Specific Purpose Committees in 2021.
James Dimon is Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer; the Chair and CEO roles are combined.

The Board determined that combining the Chair and CEO roles is the most effective leadership structure at this time, and the independent directors appointed a Lead Independent Director as a counterbalance.
Stephen B. Burke is the Lead Independent Director and has served in that role since 2021.

In the March 2022 leadership review, the Governance Committee recommended re-appointing Burke as Lead Independent Director, and the independent directors determined to maintain the current structure with Burke serving as Lead Independent Director.
Stephen B. Burke has been a director since 2004.
Linda B. Bammann has been a director since 2013.
Todd A. Combs has been a director since 2016.
James S. Crown has been a director since 2004.
James Dimon has been a director since 2004.
Timothy P. Flynn has been a director since 2012.
Mellody Hobson has been a director since 2018.
Michael A. Neal has been a director since 2014.
Phebe N. Novakovic has been a director since 2020.
Virginia M. Rometty has been a director since 2020.
All directors of the Firm were elected by shareholders in 2021.
Audit Committee members: Timothy P. Flynn (Chair), Michael A. Neal and Phebe N. Novakovic.
Compensation & Management Development Committee members: Stephen B. Burke (Chair), Linda B. Bammann, Todd A. Combs and Virginia M. Rometty.
Corporate Governance & Nominating Committee members: Todd A. Combs (Chair), Stephen B. Burke and Virginia M. Rometty.
Public Responsibility Committee members: James S. Crown (Chair), Mellody Hobson and Michael A. Neal.
Risk Committee members: Linda B. Bammann (Chair), James S. Crown and Mellody Hobson.
The CMDC report was provided by the independent directors comprising the CMDC: Stephen B. Burke (Chair), Linda B. Bammann, Todd A. Combs and Virginia M. Rometty.
The Audit Committee comprised three non-management directors: Timothy P. Flynn (Chair), Michael A. Neal and Phebe N. Novakovic.
The Board determined each Audit Committee member has no material relationship with the Firm and is independent under NYSE listing standards and SEC audit committee independence standards.
The Board determined each Audit Committee member is financially literate and an audit committee financial expert as defined by the SEC.
The Board determined each 2021 Audit Committee member (Flynn, Neal, Novakovic) to be an audit committee financial expert under the SEC definition.
The Board determined that Risk Committee chair Linda B. Bammann has experience identifying, assessing and managing risk exposures of large, complex financial firms under Federal Reserve rules.
No CMDC member is or ever was a JPMorgan Chase officer or employee except Linda B. Bammann, who previously served as an officer 15 years before joining the CMDC and 8 years before joining the Board.
Three women directors were elected to the Board in the past four years, one of whom is a person of color.
